name: to_sparse
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::to_sparse(Tensor self, *, Layout? layout=None, int[2]? blocksize=None, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. Original Gems pytest owns the full contract, including every registered overload, the keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation; do not narrow its coverage to this one representative signature. Registered schemas: aten::to_sparse.sparse_dim(Tensor self, int sparse_dim) -> Tensor ; aten::to_sparse(Tensor self, *, Layout? layout=None, int[2]? blocksize=None, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. Semantics: value-preserving dense-to-sparse layout conversion of self through the single public candidate flag_gems.to_sparse; an omitted layout is the schema default (coalesced COO), layout=torch.sparse_coo produces COO while layout=torch.sparse_csr / torch.sparse_csc produce that compressed layout, the blocked targets torch.sparse_bsr / torch.sparse_bsc consume blocksize=[rows, cols], layout=torch.strided is the identity that must stay a view over the input storage (same data_ptr, stride and storage_offset), and dense_dim keeps that many trailing dense dimensions. The other registered overload instead takes a required positional sparse_dim (sparse_dim = rank - dense_dim) and cannot be combined with dense_dim; both forms are invocable through the same entrypoint. Tests also cover omitted versus explicit None keywords, already-sparse sources that must be returned unchanged (the same object when layout and blocksize already match), offset / transposed / stride-0 expanded views, zero-extent shapes, duplicate coordinates and stored zeros, special floating values, autograd relocation and accumulation, and invalid arguments that must raise RuntimeError. The representative schema records no parameter mutation and no argument alias; the strided-identity view sharing is layout-conditional and stays expressed in pytest, not as a conditional effect here.
